migration.migration_reason: A preserved paid Semantic Compression metric shard with the same scientific experiment identity as the recertified owner was rebound to the current canonical catalog. Explicit legacy fragments, when present, matched exactly; the current metric validator re-checks the result.

limitations: Common-basis figure (probes where ALL TEN languages have a fragment) cannot be computed by this single-language worker; this record reports TypeScript's all-fragments basis only (n_L = 40), as required to be published alongside the common-basis figure once all ten languages' shards are merged by the runner.

The frozen 0-100 normalization formula for Semantic Determinacy was not present among this packet's embedded inputs; the monotonic fallback transform documented above was applied and must be reconciled with the official formula (if it differs) before final aggregation across languages.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_ref: semantic_compression.md section B (Semantic Determinacy, 25% of quality score)
metric.semantic_determinacy.normalization_note: The frozen normalization/token-counting rule document referenced by capability_universe.json (methodology 02) that converts raw mean(log2(B_i)) into the final 0-100 scale was not among this packet's embedded inputs, so a documented, monotonic, symmetric fallback transform was applied identically to how it would be applied to any language: normalized_score = 100 * 2^(-mean_log2_B) = 100 / geomean(B_i). This maps a perfectly determinate language (all B_i=1, mean_log2=0) to 100 and decreases monotonically as branching grows. This is recorded as a methodology gap (blocker for exact cross-run comparability) rather than a fabricated official normalization; raw per-probe B_i and the raw mean(log2 B_i) are preserved below for re-normalization once the frozen formula is supplied.

F01.P1.basis: const n = 7; return n; -- number is always float64, const binding is always non-reassignable, initialization is unconditional; single interpretation from local form.

F01.P2.basis: let counter: number = 0; const LIMIT: number = 100; -- let vs const mutability is unambiguous and locally determined; single interpretation.

F02.P1.basis: TS strict-mode definite-assignment analysis over both branches is a single deterministic local check; single interpretation.

F02.P2.basis: new Uint8Array(16) -- ECMAScript spec guarantees typed arrays are zero-initialized (no true uninitialized storage capability in TS/JS); substitution per R9, but the substituted fragment's semantics are unambiguous (always zero-filled).

F03.P1.basis: x += 1; -- JS number arithmetic never overflows/traps, single well-defined float64 semantics.

F03.P2.basis: xs[1] = 42; -- arrays are always reference-typed objects in JS regardless of let/const of the binding; single interpretation (in-place mutation visible through xs).

F04.P2.basis: const window: readonly number[] = xs; -- no runtime copy occurs for object assignment in JS (single behavior); readonly is a compile-time-only view, a single documented mechanism.

F04.P3.basis: === on two object references is always reference/identity equality in JS, never structural, for non-primitive operands; single interpretation.

F05.P1.basis: f(x) where x is an array -- JS always passes objects by shared reference (never by value, never invisible to callee). From the bare call-site syntax alone, of the 6 listed candidate outcomes, 'callee cannot observe caller's object at all' and 'a copy was made so no caller-visible change is possible' are impossible under JS's single object-passing convention; the remaining 4 (read-only use, write elements, resize/replace, retain alias beyond call) all remain compatible with the bare call-site syntax alone.

F05.P3.basis: Arrow-function closures in JS always capture enclosing bindings by reference to the variable (not a value snapshot); single, unambiguous, spec-fixed capture semantics.

F06.P1.basis: Returned element is a primitive number; primitives are always independent values in JS, never aliases; single interpretation.

F06.P2.basis: Tuple literal [q, r] destructured via const [q, r] = divmod2(a, b); -- TS tuple typing and array destructuring are single, well-defined mechanisms.

F07.P1.basis: a * b + c on numbers -- single float64 arithmetic semantics, fixed operator precedence, no overload resolution ambiguity for the built-in number type.

F07.P2.basis: Math.trunc(a / b); a % b; a / b -- JS spec fixes truncating division via Math.trunc, remainder sign follows the dividend, and / is already real division since numbers are always float64; single interpretation.

F08.P2.basis: b === 0 ? 0 : Math.trunc(a / b) -- explicit local guard (rung ii, since no standard checked-division op exists); single deterministic outcome.

F09.P1.basis: s1 === s2 on primitive strings is always content/value equality in JS (strings are primitives), never object identity; single interpretation.

F09.P2.basis: xs.sort((a,b)=>b-a) -- Array.prototype.sort is documented to sort in place and return the same array; single behavior. a < b is ordinary numeric comparison, single semantics.

F10.P1.basis: big | 0 -- JS bitwise OR with 0 performs the spec-defined ToInt32 abstract operation, a single deterministic wraparound-truncation rule (rung ii, explicit syntax).

F10.P2.basis: i + d -- both operands are already the single JS number (float64) type; no conversion syntax exists or is needed; single interpretation.

F11.P1.basis: xs[i] -- ECMAScript spec fixes out-of-range array indexing to return undefined (never throws); single actual runtime behavior, though the static number type masks it (a Hidden-Semantic-Cost concern, not a determinacy branching concern).

F11.P2.basis: xs.slice(1,4) -- Array.prototype.slice is documented to return a shallow copy; single behavior.

F12.P1.basis: o ?? 0 -- the nullish-coalescing operator has a single fixed semantics (substitutes only on null/undefined).

F12.P2.basis: No standard optional-map operator exists for a plain number|undefined union (R9 substitution, PARTIAL under P-a): o === undefined ? undefined : h(o) -- a single deterministic ternary form.

F13.P2.basis: try { ... } catch { n = 0 } -- standard try/catch has a single, well-defined local-handling semantics.

F14.P1.basis: type Shape = Circle | Rect discriminated union -- single, standard, well-understood TS idiom; the union alias cannot gain a member from outside its own declaration.

F14.P2.basis: switch on discriminant with no default arm, function must return a value on every path -- TS's control-flow 'not all code paths return a value' check indirectly enforces exhaustiveness; single deterministic check.

F14.P3.basis: interface Named { area(): number } with Tri implementing it from a separate module and dispatched through the interface type -- JS/TS method calls are always singly, dynamically dispatched; single interpretation.

F15.P1.basis: function head<T>(xs: T[]): T -- TS generics preserve the exact declared type relationship between parameter and result; single interpretation.

F15.P2.basis: function maxOf<T extends number>(a: T, b: T): T -- bound is explicit at the declaration; single interpretation (support level recorded separately as PARTIAL under P-a since TS lacks a general Comparable/Ord abstraction).

F15.P3.basis: const items: Named[] = [new A(), new B()]; items[0].tag() -- always dynamically dispatched through the object's own method table; single interpretation.

F16.P1.basis: xs.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0) -- Array.prototype.reduce has single documented left-to-right fold semantics.

F16.P2.basis: Map iteration is spec-guaranteed insertion order; mp.get('b') on an absent key is spec-guaranteed to return undefined, coalesced with ??; single interpretation for both facts.

F17.P1.basis: try { ... } finally { close() } -- finally is spec-guaranteed to run exactly once on every exit path including thrown exceptions; single interpretation. (ES2023 'using' is unavailable under the frozen es2022 target.)

F17.P2.basis: Explicit dispose() pattern invoked inside try/finally -- JS/TS has no automatic deterministic finalizer (FinalizationRegistry is explicitly documented as non-deterministic and not to be relied upon), so the manual dispose-in-finally idiom is used; the finally-guaranteed single call is itself unambiguous.

F18.P1.basis: console.log('x') -- console is a global available without any import statement in both Node and browser hosts under the frozen recipe; single interpretation.

F18.P2.basis: export function pubAdd / non-exported function secret in util.ts, imported via 'import { pubAdd } from ./util' -- TS/ES module export visibility is a single, compiler-enforced rule.

F19.P1.basis: const [a,b] = await Promise.all([task1(), task2()]) -- Promise.all has a single documented join semantics (waits for both, preserves argument order in the result array) regardless of completion order.

F19.P2.basis: Two async functions each synchronously incrementing a shared counter 1000 times with no await inside the loop -- JS's run-to-completion / single-threaded execution model is a normative ECMAScript guarantee that a synchronous code region between suspension points cannot be interleaved with another job; this yields a single deterministic race-free interpretation without any explicit lock construct.

metric.semantic_determinacy.raw_formula: mean(log2(B_i)) over probes for which TypeScript has a fragment (FULL or PARTIAL). Lower raw value = better (more determinate).
